section.title: Workbench sessions
section.empty: No sessions yet. Start one with +.

unpushedTooltip: {{count}} commit(s) on this branch are not pushed to a remote

newSession.title: New worktree session
newSession.description: Creates a git worktree on its own branch and starts the agent in it.

actions.worktreeMissing: The worktree folder no longer exists.

merge.title: Squash-merge into base branch
merge.body: This squashes {{branch}} into one commit on {{base}} in your main working copy.
merge.requirements: The main working copy must be on the base branch and have no uncommitted changes, and this worktree must be committed. On conflicts the merge is aborted.

discard.title: Discard this session?
discard.body: This permanently deletes the worktree folder and its branch. It cannot be undone.
discard.commits: {{count}} commit(s) not merged into the base branch will be lost

hooks.title: Status hooks
hooks.explain: Workbench can show when an agent is waiting for you or finished. To do that, each CLI gets small hooks in its own user-level config. Nothing is changed until you confirm for that CLI.
hooks.pointFile: Merged into {{path}}; nothing else in the file is changed.
hooks.pointBackup: A timestamped backup of the file is made first.
hooks.pointScoped: The hook does nothing outside Workbench sessions.
hooks.pointRemove: You can remove it again here at any time.
hooks.fallback: Without hooks, Workbench still guesses from terminal activity.

claude.explain: Adds Notification, Stop and UserPromptSubmit hooks to Claude Code.

codex.trustNote: After installing, open Codex once and run /hooks to trust the new hooks; Codex skips untrusted hooks.

notifications.waitingBody: The agent on {{branch}} is waiting for you.
